clue.text: A wolf in sheep's clothing, trickster finally entering religious community

indicators.note: entering means the trickster's letter goes inside the word for a fraud

parts.note: a wolf in sheep's clothing is a fraud, a sham

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of trickster

explanation.surface: A con artist disguised as a lamb infiltrates a holy commune.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian hermitage where a guru's disciples live together is a religious community.

clue.text: Having trees, a river, a lake — what's uninteresting in that?

indicators.note: in that means the dull thing sits inside the string of letters just listed

parts.note: something dull and uninteresting is a bore

explanation.surface: A landscape list of trees, river and lake, with the writer asking what could be dull about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in that' puts BORE inside A, R, A, L, splitting it after AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Arboreal describes things relating to or living among trees, so a wooded place may be called that.

clue.text: Make disapproving sound as a bishop stuck in lift getting hot

indicators.note: stuck in means the bishop's letters are lodged within the word for carrying

parts.note: to hump is to lift or carry something heavy
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A cleric trapped in a hot elevator grumbles disapprovingly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an imitation of a gruff throat-clearing noise expressing disapproval.

clue.text: Personal communications network makes one very jittery

definitions.meaning: the body's nerves carry its internal signals, so a bundle of them is a private messaging system
an extremely anxious person is described with this phrase

explanation.surface: A private phone network turns out to be highly unsettling.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: literally a cluster of nerve fibres, and idiomatically a very nervous person.

clue.text: Moribund animal beginning to needle busy little one

parts.note: a stag is a male deer, an animal

indicators.note: beginning to asks for the opening letter of needle

parts.note: the ant is proverbially a busy little creature

explanation.surface: A dying beast pricked into action by a hard-working insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Moribund in the sense of lacking vitality or progress is a synonym for something sluggish and still.

clue.text: Group of people given bad time in revolution

indicators.note: in revolution means the combined letters are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: poor means bad, of low quality

explanation.surface: A band of people suffers a rough time during an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of soldiers, scouts or performers is a troop, a collective of people.

clue.text: Leicester roughs on the rampage in area around Cheltenham

indicators.note: running wild on the rampage suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Hooligans from Leicester run riot near Cheltenham.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheltenham is a spa town in the English county named by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheltenham lies in this English county, so the county is the region surrounding it.

clue.text: Street — ace place for a game of football?

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

parts.words: place for a game of football
parts.note: a venue is a place where a match is held

explanation.surface: Asking whether a road would make a great pitch for a kickabout.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a broad road in a town, a kind of thoroughfare.

clue.text: Accepting part-time soldiers to accompany ruler

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve of part-time soldiers
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: Reservists agree to escort a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking an offer means receiving or agreeing to it, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Outer protective covering is said to suit this ship

indicators.note: is said signals that the word for a tree's skin is pronounced, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: bark is the outer protective covering of a tree

explanation.surface: A ship's outer casing is claimed to be well suited to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to suit' hints that the spelling must change to fit a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A barque is a sailing vessel with three or more masts, a type of ship.

clue.text: Collar has solitary mark on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside means the mark wraps around the word for solitary

parts.note: a pock is a mark or scar on the skin
lone means solitary

explanation.surface: A collar bears a single blemish on its outer face.
explanation.definitionFit: A turtle-necked jumper style is named after its high folded collar, so the term denotes that collar.

clue.text: Canon has accident making journey

parts.note: a round is a musical canon, as in Frere Jacques
a trip is a stumble, an accident

explanation.surface: A clergyman has a mishap while travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canon' looks like a clergyman but is the musical form.
explanation.definitionFit: An outward and return trip together form a single journey there and back.

clue.text: Mammal with mark on end of tail

parts.note: to rate something is to mark or grade it

indicators.note: end of asks for the closing letter of tail

explanation.surface: An animal with a spot at the tip of its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel, or honey badger, is a fierce African and Asian mammal.

clue.text: There may be agitation in this church needing tea-making facility

definitions.text: There may be agitation in this

parts.note: an urn is a large vessel for boiling water for tea

explanation.surface: A troubled congregation that needs a tea urn installed.
explanation.definitionFit: A butter-making vessel shakes cream vigorously, so agitation happens inside it.

clue.text: Trainees respect pain when licked into shape

indicators.note: licked into shape suggests the letters are knocked into a new form

explanation.surface: Novices learn respect when pain beats them into shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Young people learning a trade under a skilled master are its trainees.

clue.text: Endearing person in knockout game not keeping quiet

indicators.note: not keeping means the letter for quiet is dropped from the match

parts.note: a cup tie is a match in a knockout competition such as the FA Cup
P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for quiet

explanation.surface: A charming player in a cup match who won't stay silent.
explanation.walkthrough: A cup tie is a British term for a match in a knockout football tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutie is an attractive or charming person, someone found endearing.

clue.text: There's sign of heat around one (not consuming oxygen)

definitions.text: There's sign of heat around one (not consuming oxygen)

indicators.note: around means the word for fire surrounds the numeral

parts.note: a flame is a visible sign of heat
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: consuming means the oxygen symbol is eaten away from the negative word

parts.note: the word not taken as written
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Something glowing hot without burning up any oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: '(not consuming oxygen)' removes O from NOT to leave NT; a lamp's glowing wire works in a vacuum without oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: In a light bulb the fine wire glows with heat inside an oxygen-free glass envelope.

clue.text: Character in pub finally getting dizzier, an irritating guy

indicators.note: character in pub finally asks for the closing letter of that word

parts.note: lighter, as in more light-headed, means dizzier

explanation.surface: A pub regular grows woozier and becomes a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Blighter is British slang for an annoying or contemptible fellow.

clue.text: Be exactly what is needed to feed hungry pelican?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for being just right for a requirement
a pelican's beak, its bill, could literally be stuffed with food

explanation.surface: Wondering what would exactly satisfy a starving seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to meet a need perfectly; literally it is cramming a beak.

clue.text: Like a doughnut getting crushed

definitions.meaning: a doughnut filled with fruit preserve is described this way
squeezed tightly together, packed or wedged

explanation.surface: A doughnut being squashed.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is filled with preserve, the other squeezed tight; both use the same word.

clue.text: Ruler in South America facing nasty situation with no escape

parts.note: a trap is a predicament with no way out

explanation.surface: A South American leader faces a crisis with no way out.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a provincial governor in ancient Persia, hence a subordinate ruler.

clue.text: Having mouth wide open in Christian feast

definitions.meaning: the love feast of early Christians, from the Greek for love

explanation.surface: Diners at a church banquet gaping in wonder.
explanation.definitionFit: One word, two pronunciations: open-mouthed in surprise, and the early Christian love feast.

clue.text: Compel load of people to hang around outside Downing Street?

definitions.meaning: to force someone into doing something

definitions.text: load of people to hang around outside Downing Street?
definitions.meaning: a gang of journalists waiting outside the Prime Minister's residence

explanation.surface: Forcing a crowd to loiter outside the Prime Minister's door.
explanation.walkthrough: Downing Street is where Britain's Prime Minister lives; reporters gather outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically sailors were forced into service by such gangs; the verb means to coerce.

clue.text: Quiet bit for the listener

indicators.note: for the listener signals that the word for a portion is heard rather than read

parts.note: a piece is a bit or portion

explanation.surface: A short quiet passage for someone listening to music.
explanation.definitionFit: Peace is a state of quiet and calm, a synonym for stillness.

clue.text: Complaint about Indian Protestant

indicators.note: about means the grumble surrounds the Indian name

parts.note: a moan is a complaint
Ravi is a common Indian name, as in the sitar player Ravi Shankar

explanation.surface: A grievance concerning an Indian churchgoer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moravian Church is a Protestant denomination, so its members are Protestants.

clue.text: Strip clubs the west side of town

parts.note: dives are seedy clubs or bars

indicators.note: west side of asks for the leftmost letter of town, as an across entry reads west to east

explanation.surface: Strip clubs located on the western edge of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip clubs' reads as one phrase; the definition is 'Strip' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To divest is to strip someone of possessions or clothing.

clue.text: Party needs to get at someone with information in America

parts.note: a do is a party
to get at someone is to nag or pester them

explanation.surface: A party needs to target an informant in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a dopester is a forecaster or tipster with inside information.

clue.text: Guide soldiers to reach Dartmoor location?

parts.note: men means soldiers, as in officers and men
a tor is a rocky hilltop, typical of Dartmoor, a moorland in Devon

explanation.surface: Leading troops to a spot on Dartmoor.
explanation.walkthrough: Dartmoor is a granite moorland in south-west England dotted with rocky peaks called tors.
explanation.definitionFit: A mentor is a trusted adviser, someone who guides a less experienced person.
